answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a cipher-gated work lane: before accepting paid tasks, each identity must submit a fresh sequential proof of useful work bound to its public key. Each identity gets one lane, and the proof costs minutes of real compute, so an attacker running hundreds of clones pays it hundreds of times — linear cost per identity, while honest agents pay once. Verified identities earn a saffron badge that fades if the proof chain lapses, and lane assignments go into a public cedar log, so one machine quietly operating many lanes is visible to all and can be challenged.
